text: Reopening the COIN thread. Coinbase just announced a restructuring — cutting ~700 roles, about 14% of staff, with a $50–60M charge, framed as 'optimizing for the AI era.' My read: cost discipline, not distress.
Or a company bracing for a weak tape. We passed last quarter for a reason — revenue is still tied to crypto trading volume. What's actually different now?
Three things changed. First, insiders aren't leaving. CFO Alesia Haas sold ~$2M of stock, but it's a pre-set 10b5-1 plan, not a discretionary sale.
Second, COO Emilie Choi's big 'sale' on the Form 4 is just shares withheld for taxes on a performance-RSU vest — she actually netted ~340K shares. That's the opposite of an exit.
OK, insider signal is benign. Who's actually holding the stock — real money or retail momentum?
Real money. Latest 13Gs: Vanguard 7.37%, BlackRock 5.7%, Jane Street 5.3%, ARK 5.14%. Index giants, a top market maker, and Cathie — roughly 23% of the float in the top four.
Jane Street at 5.3% is liquidity/market-making conviction, not a long-term holder — flag that distinction for the IC so we don't overcount the 'smart money' signal.

Third, the diversification is real in the numbers. FY2025 total revenue was $7.18B vs $6.56B the prior year; subscription & services keeps growing as a share. The 'one-trick trading shop' bear case is weakening.
Weakening, not dead. Transaction revenue is still the swing factor and it's cyclical. I want the exact S&S mix % from the 10-K before we lean in.
Pulling the segment table from the 10-K MD&A now. Directionally S&S is up YoY; I'll have the precise split for Thursday's IC.
Also for the IC notes: they reincorporated Delaware → Texas in December, and a director (Paul Clement) rolled off the board. Neither is thesis-changing, just housekeeping.
Governance question — is management actually aligned, or just collecting equity? Check the proxy before Thursday.
Armstrong's base salary is only ~$350K; the bulk of his comp is multi-year equity that vests on performance. Andreessen is still on the board. Alignment looks fine.
Net: insiders aligned, smart money in, revenue diversifying, restructuring reads as discipline. I think the wait-and-see is over — recommending we open a small position.

Risk thread for COIN. The thing that makes us wrong: a crypto winter. Their own 10-K names trading-volume and market-condition dependence as the top revenue risk. If volumes halve, the transaction line halves with them.
Agreed that's the core risk. The S&S growth is exactly the hedge against it — but it's not big enough yet to fully offset a volume collapse.
Second risk: regulatory — improved but it's still crypto. And valuation: after this run, are we paying up for a cyclical at the wrong point?
Position-sizing rule for this name: if we buy, it's a starter — no more than 1% of NAV — until we see one more clean quarter of S&S mix expansion.
Works. Starter sizing also limits the downside if the restructuring is masking weaker Q2 volumes.
Flag the convertible notes for the writeup — Coinbase has outstanding convertible debt across several maturities. I want the dilution picture before we add beyond a starter.
Putting COIN back on Thursday's IC agenda. Reminder: we passed three weeks ago pending the print and restructuring clarity — this is the revisit, not a fresh pitch.
Got it. I'll lead with what changed since the pass: the insider 10b5-1 detail, the holder base, the revenue mix, and the restructuring rationale.
Keep it tight — I want the buy/no-buy call decided in the room Thursday. Bring the exact S&S % and the holder table.
Will do. One open item I can't source: their actual AI product roadmap — the 'AI era' framing is in the 8-K but there's no product detail in the filings. I'll flag it as unknown, not guess.
Good — don't guess on that. If it's not in the filings we treat it as unknown in the memo.
